title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 109-112, §VII-VIII of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck is studying the twisted 'loop equation' g·ρ(g)·ρ²(g) = 1 in SL(2,Ẑ) (and GL(2,Ẑ)). Here ρ denotes an automorphism of order 3, namely conjugation by an element of order 3 (or 6) such as (0 -1; 1 -1). In modern terms, a solution is a 1-cocycle of Z/3 acting on SL(2,Ẑ), and elements of the form λ0·ρ(λ0)^{-1} are the coboundaries. The problem behind this is the SL2 / 'abelianized' shadow of the order-3 relation that elements of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller type must satisfy on π1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, i.e. f(x,y)f(y,z)f(z,x)=1 with xyz=1. Earlier formulas (78) parametrize the solutions ξ = (A B; C D) according to cases. These cases are described by 'primitives', which appear to be the solutions of an auxiliary equation. The general case has two primitives (2-parameter family). The other cases give 1- and 0-parameter families, as stated on p.110. On p.110 he admits he does not know whether every cocycle is of the form λ0 ρ(λ0)^{-1} (or a twisted variant λ0' τ0 ρ(λ0')^{-1}). He notes this can be tested separately in each SL(2,Z_ℓ), with a possible obstruction at ℓ=2 (the condition g ≡ id mod 2). On this page he records three things. (i) If ξ = λ0 ρ(λ0)^{-1}, then ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 automatically, and the formulas (78) give the linear relation C+D−B = 1. So coboundaries fall in the 'general' case with two primitives. (ii) A crossed-out remark: the twisted form g = λ0(…)ρ(λ0)^{-1} would land in case B), with c+d−b = −1, again a two-primitive case. The marginal note says 'ok, cf. … ci-dessous'. (iii) One must exclude the degenerate case A+B = 0. A crossed-out line identifies a particular instance with ξ = −ρ^{-1} = (−1 1; −1 0). The degenerate case is case 2 of the primitives, ξ = (−u u; C −u'−C), with u a primitive cube root of unity and u' = u^{-1} = u². One checks det ξ = u(u'+C) − uC = uu' = 1. The next page passes to the analogous computation for the involution σ∞ = (0 -1; 1 0), where conjugation is the contragredient and h σ∞(h) = 1 iff h is symmetric. Overall the page is a bookkeeping step in computing nonabelian H^1(Z/3, SL(2,Ẑ)) for the order-3 automorphism, i.e. deciding which cocycles are coboundaries.
errors: Over Ẑ itself there is no primitive cube root of unity. x²+x+1 has no root in Z_2 (it is irreducible mod 2) and none in Z_3 (−3 is not a square in Q_3). So 'case 2' with u a primitive cube root of 1 is empty in SL(2,Ẑ). It can only occur componentwise in Z_ℓ for ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3, consistent with his remark on p.110 to argue ℓ by ℓ. The page does not note this; possibly 'racine' is meant in a different sense, so uncertain.
The derivation of C+D−B = 1 from (78) is asserted, not shown on this page. It cannot be checked without formulas (78), but it is consistent with the case analysis on p.110.
The crossed-out statement (c+d−b = −1 for the twisted coboundary) is explicitly left uncomputed ('je me dispense de faire le calcul ici') and then cancelled.

ideas.what: Solutions of gρ(g)ρ²(g)=1 viewed as 1-cocycles of Z/3 acting on SL(2,Ẑ) via an order-3 inner automorphism; checking whether a cocycle is a coboundary λ0ρ(λ0)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian group cohomology H^1(Z/3, SL2(Ẑ)); the order-3 (hexagon-type) relation of GT, reduced to the SL2 / level-structure quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nonabelian H^1: Serre / Grothendieck (classical). GT relations: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara 1990s.
ideas.where_published: The general program is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The SL2 computations belong to La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, manuscript), not formally published.

ideas.what: Case analysis of solutions by 'primitives' (2-, 1-, 0-parameter families). Coboundaries satisfy a linear relation C+D−B=1 and lie in the general case; the degenerate case A+B=0 involves a primitive cube root of unity.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit parametrization of order-3 twisted cocycles in SL2 over a profinite ring
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; elementary matrix computation

ideas.what: Reduction of the coboundary question to each SL(2,Z_ℓ) separately, with special behaviour at ℓ=2 (stated on the neighbouring page)
ideas.modern_name: Local-to-global (prime-by-prime) analysis of profinite nonabelian cohomology

missed.claim: The question of whether every solution of ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 in SL(2,Ẑ) is a (twisted) coboundary is left open across pp.110-111. Here he only verifies the necessary linear condition and excludes a degenerate case. This would amount to computing H^1(Z/3, SL2(Ẑ)) for this action, which is doable and probably known in substance from the theory of torsion in SL2(Z) and its profinite completion. So it is not really new.
missed.quote: on aura C+D−B=1 — i.e. dans le cas "général" à deux primitives ... nous excluons le cas A+B=0 ... i.e. le cas 2 des primitives
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a toy version of the image of GT-type relations in SL2(Ẑ). It is of mild interest for understanding the image of Ĝ T or of Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on level structures, but likely routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an intermediate bookkeeping step in an explicit matrix computation of order-3 cocycles in SL(2,Ẑ), part of the known Longue Marche program. It contains no new construction or unexpected connection beyond what the program as a whole (anticipating GT relations) is already known for.

The crossed-out block reads approximately 'que si je prends g = λ0(…)ρ(λ0)^{-1}, on sera dans le cas B), avec c+d−b=−1, i.e. le cas 1°) encore à deux primitives. Je me dispense de faire le calcul ici'.
The margin note reads 'ok, cf. (??) ci-dessous', with a reference number (possibly (89) or (99)) that is hard to read.
